textbookText: Let’s study a case According to a news published on 6th September 2023 in the newspaper ‘my Republica’, About 42000 people die because of the effect of air pollution every year in Nepal and according to WHO, Kathmandu is placed 96th rank among the most polluted cities in the world. The same newspaper which published a news article on 16th April stated that Kathmandu had become the first in the list of most polluted cities in the world in terms of air pollution on Saturday evening. Different kind of non-communicable diseases are emerging because of this situation. According to an environmentalist, from the United Nations Development Commission on clean air, Madhesh Pradesh is also experiencing more pollution because of various industries present there. Polluted air consists of several harmful substances or pollutants such as CO, CO2 harmful gases and carcinogens. Such substances are circulated throughout the body with blood and affect various organs including lungs. Because of the effect of air pollution, Average life expectancy of Nepalese has been decreased by 4.6 years. For the past few years, such pollution related news has been publishing from time to time in Nepal. This is only a sample news item.

Discuss the questions given below on the basis of given case: i. What might be the causes of aforementioned condition in Kathmandu? ii. What are the current health issues faced by animals and plants including human beings due to such situations? iii. What role can be played to control this condition on your behalf?

The word pollution is derived from a latin word pollutionem which means ‘defilement’. Simply, pollution is the introduction of harmful substances to the environment. Such activity results degradation of natural or original quality of various environmental components. The causes of pollution are natural and anthropogenic both. Anthropogenic causes include various type of human intrusion on the nature such as industrial activities, using excessive pesticides and chemical fertilizer in agricultural land, fossil fuel combustion, and unsystematic disposal of municipal and industrial wastes, deforestation and increasing urbanization. Similarly, natural causes are volcanic eruptions, forest fire, dust storms, decay of dead organic matter, pollens etc. Environmental pollution is now being a global burning issue and posing a serious threat to flora and fauna including human beings. Pollution causes different types of health disorders in human such as asthma, bronchitis, poor mental health, anaemia, COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease), blood pressure etc.

Human population is increasing day by day and it obviously demand for more food, transportation, water supply, road, housings, hospital, vehicles electricity and more industrial products. Its consequences are depletion and degradation of natural resources. To conclude, pollution is any undesirable changes in the physical, chemical and biological characteristics of the environment. Any substances that make the environment dirty and polluted are called pollutants. TYPES OF POLLUTANTS On this basis of changing or unchanged nature of pollutants, they are of two types:
a. Primary pollutant: Those pollutants which remain in the same form as they are discharged from the sources to the environment. Example: DDT, fly ash etc.

b. Secondary pollutant: Pollutants which are formed by the chemical combination of primary pollutants. They are more toxic than primary pollutants. Example: smog, peroxy-acetyl nitrate (PAN), ozone etc.

On the basis of degrading or non-degrading nature of pollutants, they are of two types: a. Degradable pollutants: such pollutants which degrade or decompose in nature quite rapidly by the action of microbes and heat. Example: biological or organic wastes.
b. Non degradable pollutants: such pollutants which do not degrade or decompose in nature are called non-degradable wastes. Example: DDT, BHC, plastic, tin can etc.

9.3.2 AIR POLLUTION Normal composition of atmospheric air is 78.08% nitrogen, 20.95% oxygen, 0.93% argon, 0.04% carbon dioxide, 0.4% water vapour and remaining amount other gases. Various chemicals, smoke, particles, gases etc. are released to the atmosphere by both manmade and natural cause resulting in the alteration of natural quality of atmosphere which is air pollution. Air pollution impacts adversely on the status of natural resources, health of plants, animals including human beings. Any substances polluting or altering the originality of air are called air pollutants.
